title: World's first Pendolino train to enter regular high-speed service between Milan and Rome.
text: Pendolino is an Italian family of high-speed tilting trains (and non-tilting) used in Italy, Spain, Germany, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Finland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia (operated by Czech railways), the UK, the US, Switzerland, China, and Greece. It was also used in Russia from December 12, 2010, until March 26, 2022.

title: In an air show at the US Ramstein Air Base in Germany, three jets from the Italian air demonstration team, Frecce Tricolori, collide, sending a fireball into the ground. All three pilots and 67 spectators are killed, with a further 346…
text: On 28 August 1988, three aircraft of the Italian Air Force display team collided during the Flugtag '88 airshow at USAF Ramstein Air Base near Kaiserslautern, West Germany. They crashed to the ground in front of a crowd of about 300,000 people, causing 70 fatalities; 346 spectators sustained serious injuries in the resulting explosion and fire.

title: 1988 San Marino Grand Prix
text: The 1988 San Marino Grand Prix was a Formula One motor race held at Imola on 1 May 1988. The 60-lap race was the second round of the 1988 Formula One season.

title: 1988 Italian motorcycle Grand Prix
text: The 1988 Nations motorcycle Grand Prix was the fifth race of the 1988 Grand Prix motorcycle racing season. It took place on the weekend of 20–22 May 1988, at the Autodromo Dino Ferrari.

title: 1988 Italian Open (tennis)
text: The 1988 Italian Open was a tennis tournament played on outdoor clay courts at the Foro Italico in Rome in Italy, that was part of the 1988 Nabisco Grand Prix and of Tier IV of the 1988 WTA Tour. The men's tournament was held from 9 May until 15 May 1988, while the women's tournament was held from 2 May until 8 May 1988.

title: “La Bamba” by Los Lobos
text: "La Bamba" is a Mexican folk song, originally from the state of Veracruz. The song is best known from a 1958 adaptation by Ritchie Valens, a top 40 hit on the U.S. charts.

title: “Pump Up the Volume” by MARRS
text: "Pump Up the Volume" is the only single by British recording act M|A|R|R|S. The song was written by Martyn Young and Steve Young, and produced by the former and John Fryer. It was recorded in 1987 and released on 3 August of the same year.

title: “Sì, la vita è tutta un quiz” by Renzo Arbore
text: Lorenzo Giovanni "Renzo" Arbore is an Italian television host, singer, actor and film director.

title: “Perdere l'amore” by Massimo Ranieri
text: "Perdere l'amore" is a 1988 song composed by Marcello Marrocchi and Giampiero Artegiani and performed by singer Massimo Ranieri. The song won the 38th edition of the Sanremo Music Festival, and marked the return to music of Ranieri after a decade devoted to acting.

title: “L'amore rubato” by Luca Barbarossa
text: Luca Barbarossa is an Italian singer-songwriter who has released 12 albums since 1981, and is known for his participation in the 1988 Eurovision Song Contest.

title: “I'm Not Scared” by Eighth Wonder
text: "I'm Not Scared" is a song by British pop band Eighth Wonder, released in February 1988 by CBS Records International as the first single from their debut album, Fearless. The song achieved success in Europe, peaking at number seven on the UK Singles Chart, reaching number one in Italy, and entering the top five in Finland, Luxembourg, Spain, Switzerland and West Germany.

title: “Gimme Five” by Jovanotti
text: Lorenzo Cherubini, known professionally as Jovanotti (Italian: ), is an Italian singer-songwriter, rapper, and disc jockey. The name Jovanotti derives from giovanotti, the plural form of the Italian word giovanotto ("young man").

title: “Tell Me” by Nick Kamen
text: Ivor Neville "Nick" Kamen was a British singer, songwriter and model. He was best known for the singles "Each Time You Break My Heart" from 1986 and "I Promised Myself" from 1990, as well as for appearing in a 1985 Levi's advert.

title: “I Don't Want Your Love” by Duran Duran
text: "I Don't Want Your Love" is a song by the English pop rock band Duran Duran, released on 19 September 1988 as the first single from their fifth studio album, Big Thing.
listen: I Don't Want Your Love Duran Duran

title: “Desire” by U2
text: "Desire" is a song by Irish rock band U2 and the third track on their 1988 album Rattle and Hum. It was released as the album's lead single on 19 September 1988 by Island Records, and became the band's first number-one single in Australia and on the United Kingdom Singles Chart.

title: “C'è da spostare una macchina” by Francesco Salvi
text: Francesco Salvi is an Italian actor, singer, screenwriter, and director.
